note: Starter problem chart for the Gap Briefs section: six problems per sector, qualitative only, no figures. Ids (for example eng-1) become gp-eng-1 in the workspace. A sector's problem is rotated each issue: the least recently used one is picked.

problems.problem: Skilled engineers are scarce and the good ones are off the market within days.
problems.impact: Projects and contracts slip, overtime and agency spend rise, and the team left behind carries the load.
problems.root_cause: Multi-stage hiring processes that move slower than the candidate, and no pipeline built ahead of demand.
problems.questions:
How long has your longest open technical role been open?
How many engineers will you need to hire before March?
If a key engineer resigned tomorrow, how long would it take to replace them?

problems.problem: Experienced engineers are retiring faster than apprentices and graduates replace them.
problems.impact: Know-how leaves the building and projects lose their most reliable people.
problems.root_cause: No succession plan or structured handover, and weak links with colleges and apprenticeship routes.
problems.questions:
How many of your engineers are within five years of retiring?
Who would take over their work today?
How many apprentices or graduates have you brought in over the last two years?

problems.problem: Offers lose to higher pay elsewhere.
problems.impact: Engineers are poached after training, and replacing them costs more than a raise would.
problems.root_cause: Salary bands not reviewed against the market, and no clear progression.
problems.questions:
When did you last benchmark engineering pay?
Who have you lost to a competitor in the last year?
What path do engineers see ahead of them here?

problems.problem: Job descriptions ask for a perfect match, so good candidates screen themselves out.
problems.impact: Long vacancies and shortlists of near-identical people.
problems.root_cause: Requirement lists copied from the last hire instead of built from the real work.
problems.questions:
Which requirements on your last advert did the successful hire not meet?
How many are truly essential?
How long did that role stay open?

problems.problem: Contractors fill gaps for years and permanent hiring is put off.
problems.impact: Day rates cost far more than a salary and knowledge walks out at contract end.
problems.root_cause: Permanent roles seen as too slow to fill, so contract becomes the default.
problems.questions:
How many contractors have been with you for over a year?
What do you pay compared with a permanent salary?
What stops you converting them?

problems.problem: New starters take months to become productive because onboarding is informal.
problems.impact: Weeks of lost output and early leavers.
problems.root_cause: No structured first 90 days and no named buddy.
problems.questions:
How long until a new engineer works unsupervised?
Who owns onboarding?
How many starters left in their first six months?

problems.problem: Production and shop-floor roles stay unfilled while orders grow.
problems.impact: Lost output, constant overtime, and quality and safety risk from stretched shifts.
problems.root_cause: Generic adverts that do not sell shift patterns, training or progression, and limited reach beyond the immediate area.
problems.questions:
How many production roles are open right now, and for how long?
How much of your shift cover is agency, and what does it cost you?
How many starters in the last year left within three months?

problems.problem: Shift patterns put candidates off.
problems.impact: Night and weekend vacancies stay open and existing staff are stretched.
problems.root_cause: Rotas designed around the machine rather than the people, and not shown clearly in the advert.
problems.questions:
Which shifts are hardest to fill?
Have you reviewed shift patterns in the last year?
What do leavers say about them?

problems.problem: High turnover in the first weeks of employment.
problems.impact: Constant recruitment and repeated training cost.
problems.root_cause: Candidates not shown the job, site or pace before they start, and a poor first week.
problems.questions:
What share of starters leave within 90 days?
Do candidates visit site before accepting?
What does a first week look like?

problems.problem: Skilled setters, maintenance staff and technicians are in very short supply.
problems.impact: Machines stand idle when a fault needs a specialist.
problems.root_cause: Too few trained locally, and no in-house development route.
problems.questions:
How long has your longest machine downtime been, waiting for an engineer?
Do you train from within?
Who covers when your one specialist is away?

problems.problem: Heavy reliance on agency labour for core production.
problems.impact: Higher cost per hour, less skill continuity and weaker quality.
problems.root_cause: Permanent hiring too slow to meet peaks, so agency becomes the default.
problems.questions:
What share of the floor is agency?
Which agency workers would you hire permanently?
What does the premium cost you over a year?

problems.problem: Supervisors and team leaders are promoted without training.
problems.impact: Productivity, morale and safety slip under inexperienced leaders.
problems.root_cause: The best operator is promoted by default, with no leadership development.
problems.questions:
How many team leaders have had leadership training?
What happened to your last promoted operator?
Who is your next supervisor?

problems.problem: Buyers who combine commercial skill with supply chain resilience experience are hard to find.
problems.impact: Supplier risk goes unmanaged, savings are missed and negotiations are weaker.
problems.root_cause: A small candidate pool in which the strongest people are passive and never see a job board.
problems.questions:
Which buying or supply chain role has been hardest to fill?
What did the last supplier disruption cost you in time or money?
Who covers if your lead buyer is away for a month?

problems.problem: Supplier disruption exposes a team with no resilience planning.
problems.impact: Stock-outs, price spikes and emergency buying.
problems.root_cause: Buyers measured on unit price rather than risk, with single-source suppliers.
problems.questions:
Which of your inputs has a single supplier?
How quickly could you switch?
When did you last stress-test the supply base?

problems.problem: Procurement is seen as a cost centre, so pay lags other commercial roles.
problems.impact: The best buyers leave for competitors or other functions.
problems.root_cause: Value not reported to the board, so the salary budget is tight.
problems.questions:
How do you report procurement savings?
How does buyer pay compare with sales or finance?
Who has left the team in the last year?

problems.problem: Buyers lack data and systems skills.
problems.impact: Manual spreadsheets, errors and no visibility of spend.
problems.root_cause: Hiring for relationships alone, and no investment in procurement tools.
problems.questions:
How much spend sits outside your system?
Who builds the reports?
How long does a spend review take?

problems.problem: Planning and scheduling roles are left to chance.
problems.impact: Over- and under-stocking tie up cash or stop production.
problems.root_cause: Planning grew informally, with knowledge held by one person.
problems.questions:
Who would run planning if your planner left tomorrow?
How often are you short of stock?
What does excess stock cost you?

problems.problem: Category and strategic sourcing skills are missing.
problems.impact: Contracts auto-renew at old prices and opportunities are missed.
problems.root_cause: Teams stay transactional with no capacity for strategy.
problems.questions:
How many major contracts renewed without a review?
Who owns category strategy?
What was your last significant saving?

problems.problem: Strong sellers are hard to tell apart from polished interviewees, and a mis-hire is expensive and visible.
problems.impact: Quota gaps, a long ramp-up and lost pipeline when a hire does not work out.
problems.root_cause: Hiring on interview performance rather than evidence of results, with no structured check of track record.
problems.questions:
How long does a new seller take to reach full quota here?
How many sales hires in the last two years did not work out?
What happens to a territory while the seat is empty?

problems.problem: Salespeople leave within two years of starting.
problems.impact: Pipeline and client relationships walk out with them.
problems.root_cause: Territory, targets and commission are unclear or seen as unfair.
problems.questions:
How long does a seller typically stay?
What happens to their accounts when they leave?
How is commission explained at offer stage?

problems.problem: Strong sellers are hired but the ramp-up plan is vague.
problems.impact: Months of low output and unclear performance.
problems.root_cause: No structured onboarding, training or early targets.
problems.questions:
What is the plan for a new seller's first 90 days?
How many reached quota in their first six months?
Who coaches them?

problems.problem: Leads exist but are not followed up consistently.
problems.impact: Revenue is lost despite spend on marketing.
problems.root_cause: Unclear ownership between marketing and sales, and no support for first contact.
problems.questions:
What share of leads get a response within a day?
Who owns first contact?
How many go cold?

problems.problem: Technical sales is hard to staff because it needs product knowledge and selling skill together.
problems.impact: Slow quotes and lost complex deals.
problems.root_cause: Hiring for one skill and hoping to teach the other.
problems.questions:
Who supports your sellers technically?
How long do quotes take?
How many deals depend on one expert?

problems.problem: Account managers are overloaded and renewals suffer.
problems.impact: Churn and missed upsell.
problems.root_cause: Account lists grow without extra headcount.
problems.questions:
How many accounts does each manager hold?
What was last year's churn?
Who reviews your top accounts?

problems.problem: Qualified and part-qualified finance staff are in short supply, most of all around year end.
problems.impact: Late closes and audits, costly interim cover, and a team close to burnout.
problems.root_cause: Hiring starts too late against the finance calendar, and offers lose on flexibility rather than pay.
problems.questions:
Which finance seat is the one you can least afford to leave empty?
When is your next close or audit, and is the team ready for it?
Have you lost a finance candidate in the last year to a faster offer?

problems.problem: Finance teams rely on one or two people who hold all the knowledge.
problems.impact: Holiday or illness stops reporting.
problems.root_cause: Processes undocumented and no cross-training.
problems.questions:
What would break if your finance manager left?
Is month end documented?
Who can cover payroll?

problems.problem: Month end takes too long because of manual processes.
problems.impact: Late numbers and slow decisions.
problems.root_cause: Spreadsheets and rekeying in place of automation, and not enough hands.
problems.questions:
How many working days does your month end take?
Which steps are still manual?
When do managers see their numbers?

problems.problem: Credit control is understaffed, so cash arrives late.
problems.impact: Cash flow pressure and more bad debt.
problems.root_cause: Credit control treated as admin rather than a cash function.
problems.questions:
What are your average debtor days?
Who chases, and how often?
How much is over 60 days?

problems.problem: Part-qualified and newly qualified staff are hard to keep.
problems.impact: Trained people leave once they qualify.
problems.root_cause: No clear route after qualification and pay that lags the market.
problems.questions:
How many qualified in the last two years and stayed?
Where do they move on to?
What is the route after qualification here?

problems.problem: Seasonal peaks such as year end and audit overwhelm small teams.
problems.impact: Errors, stress and expensive temporary help.
problems.root_cause: Cover arranged at the last minute rather than planned.
problems.questions:
When is your next peak?
Who covers it?
What did last year's cover cost?

problems.problem: Good IT candidates hold several offers at once and decide quickly.
problems.impact: Offers declined, roles reopened and delivery dates that move.
problems.root_cause: Slow feedback between interview stages and long technical tests that candidates will not wait for.
problems.questions:
How many days pass between first interview and offer?
How many IT offers have you had turned down in the last year?
What is waiting on the next IT hire?

problems.problem: IT support is reactive and stretched.
problems.impact: Downtime, frustrated staff and security gaps left unpatched.
problems.root_cause: Too few people for the number of users and systems.
problems.questions:
How many tickets are open right now?
How long does a typical fix take?
What is not getting done because of firefighting?

problems.problem: Cyber security skills are scarce.
problems.impact: Exposure to attack and failed audits.
problems.root_cause: Security treated as an add-on with no specialist hire.
problems.questions:
Who owns security today?
When was your last test?
What would a breach cost you?

problems.problem: Developers are hired but not retained because the work is unchallenging.
problems.impact: Churn and loss of system knowledge.
problems.root_cause: Legacy systems and no modernisation roadmap.
problems.questions:
What does your oldest system run on?
How long do developers stay?
What would attract them?

problems.problem: Data and analyst roles are poorly defined.
problems.impact: Reports nobody trusts and hires who leave.
problems.root_cause: The business is unsure what it wants from data.
problems.questions:
What decision would better data change?
Who uses your reports?
What do you need the hire to deliver?

problems.problem: Remote and hybrid expectations clash with employer policy.
problems.impact: Lost candidates and mismatched expectations.
problems.root_cause: Policy set without understanding what candidates expect.
problems.questions:
What is your working policy for IT staff?
How many candidates turned you down over it?
Has it been reviewed this year?

problems.problem: Project-driven demand makes it hard to staff site and commercial roles at the right moment.
problems.impact: Programme delays, premium subcontractor rates and pressure on site safety.
problems.root_cause: Hiring reacts to awarded contracts instead of planning ahead, and travel or location puts candidates off.
problems.questions:
Which upcoming project is short of people right now?
How far ahead of a start date do you begin hiring for it?
How often does a vacancy hold up a programme milestone?

problems.problem: Estimators and quantity surveyors are in short supply.
problems.impact: Bids are late or lost and margins are mis-priced.
problems.root_cause: An ageing workforce and few entering the profession.
problems.questions:
How many bids did you pass on for lack of capacity?
How old is your estimating team?
Who is being developed?

problems.problem: Site managers are lost to competitors offering better packages.
problems.impact: Delayed projects and loss of client relationships.
problems.root_cause: Packages that ignore travel, time away and project bonuses.
problems.questions:
Who have you lost in the last year and why?
How do you handle travel time?
What is your retention plan for key managers?

problems.problem: Health and safety roles are filled late.
problems.impact: Compliance gaps and stoppages.
problems.root_cause: Compliance seen as an overhead until something goes wrong.
problems.questions:
Who is your lead for site safety?
When was your last audit?
How would you cover absence?

problems.problem: Subcontractor dependency makes programmes unpredictable.
problems.impact: Quality and cost vary from job to job.
problems.root_cause: No direct labour core to keep standards and timing.
problems.questions:
What share of your labour is subcontracted?
How many issues come from it?
Which trades could you bring in-house?

problems.problem: Graduates and apprentices are hired but not developed.
problems.impact: Wasted investment and further skills gaps.
problems.root_cause: No structured training route or mentoring on site.
problems.questions:
How many apprentices stayed after qualifying?
Who mentors them?
What is your plan for the next five years?

problems.problem: Persistent vacancies and high turnover in care and clinical teams.
problems.impact: Agency cost, broken continuity of care and compliance exposure.
problems.root_cause: Slow compliance checks between offer and start, so candidates take another job while they wait.
problems.questions:
How many care or clinical shifts went to agency last month?
How long between offer and start date for a new starter?
How many starters have you lost during the compliance stage?

problems.problem: Registered nurses and senior carers are scarce.
problems.impact: Reduced capacity, agency spend and strain on remaining staff.
problems.root_cause: Competing employers, and pay that does not reflect responsibility.
problems.questions:
How many registered posts are open?
What do you spend on agency cover?
How does your pay compare locally?

problems.problem: Care staff leave because of rotas and burnout.
problems.impact: Continuity of care suffers and recruitment never stops.
problems.root_cause: Short staffing creates long shifts, which create more leavers.
problems.questions:
What is your staff turnover?
How often do people work extra shifts?
What do exit interviews say?

problems.problem: Managers are hard to find and hard to keep.
problems.impact: Inspection risk and weak leadership.
problems.root_cause: The role carries heavy responsibility with limited support.
problems.questions:
Who covers when your manager is away?
How long was the last vacancy?
What support does your manager have?

problems.problem: Right-to-work and registration checks slow starts.
problems.impact: Offers lapse before candidates arrive.
problems.root_cause: Checks started after the offer rather than alongside it.
problems.questions:
How many weeks pass between offer and start?
Which checks hold you up?
How many accepted offers fall through?

problems.problem: Training and induction vary by site.
problems.impact: Inconsistent care and compliance gaps.
problems.root_cause: No standard induction and training records kept inconsistently.
problems.questions:
Is your induction written down?
How do you track training?
What did your last inspection say?

problems.problem: Demand for AI skills runs well ahead of supply, and role titles and skills are poorly defined.
problems.impact: Projects stall, the wrong people get hired and salary expectations climb.
problems.root_cause: Unclear role definitions and must-have lists that no real candidate matches.
problems.questions:
What exactly do you need this hire to build or own in their first six months?
How many of your must-haves would you drop for the right person?
What is on hold until this seat is filled?

problems.problem: Businesses want AI but have no one to own it.
problems.impact: Pilots stall and tools go unused.
problems.root_cause: AI treated as an IT project instead of a business capability.
problems.questions:
Who owns AI in your business?
How many pilots reached daily use?
What result do you want in a year?

problems.problem: Salary expectations for AI skills outrun budgets.
problems.impact: Offers refused and roles reopened.
problems.root_cause: Budgets set on traditional job grades.
problems.questions:
How was the salary for this role set?
How many offers have you lost over pay?
Is there flexibility for the right person?

problems.problem: Automation specialists are hired without clear processes to automate.
problems.impact: Wasted effort and poor adoption.
problems.root_cause: Processes not mapped, so there is nothing clear to improve.
problems.questions:
Which processes would you automate first?
Are they documented?
Who would benefit most?

problems.problem: Apprenticeship and entry routes into AI are underused.
problems.impact: A missed chance to grow talent affordably.
problems.root_cause: Apprenticeship funding and structure not well understood.
problems.questions:
Have you considered an AI apprentice?
What stops you?
Who would supervise them?

problems.problem: Data quality blocks AI projects.
problems.impact: Poor outputs and lost trust in the tools.
problems.root_cause: No data owner and no clean-up plan.
problems.questions:
How would you rate your data quality?
Who owns it?
What would you fix first?

problems.problem: HR teams are asked to hire quickly while still holding policy and compliance standards.
problems.impact: Time lost chasing, inconsistent process and slow hires.
problems.root_cause: Limited capacity and reactive hiring, with no consistent shortlist standard across hiring managers.
problems.questions:
How much of your week goes on chasing hiring managers and candidates?
How consistent is the process across your hiring managers?
Which vacancy is causing you the most pressure?

problems.problem: HR teams are stretched across advice, hiring and admin.
problems.impact: Strategic work never happens.
problems.root_cause: HR staffed for administration only.
problems.questions:
What share of your week is admin?
What strategic project is stuck?
Who supports you?

problems.problem: Employee relations cases take up a disproportionate share of time.
problems.impact: Hiring and development are neglected.
problems.root_cause: Managers not trained to handle issues early.
problems.questions:
How many cases are open?
How are managers trained?
What do they cost in time?

problems.problem: Learning and development is under-resourced.
problems.impact: Skills gaps and higher turnover.
problems.root_cause: Training budget is cut first and is not linked to retention.
problems.questions:
What is your training budget?
How do you track skills?
What does turnover cost you?

problems.problem: Recruitment coordination capacity is tight at peak hiring.
problems.impact: Delays in scheduling and candidate drop-out.
problems.root_cause: Admin load grows with volume but headcount stays flat.
problems.questions:
How long does it take to arrange an interview?
How many candidates drop out during the process?
Who supports your hiring managers?

problems.problem: HR systems and data are fragmented.
problems.impact: Poor reporting and compliance risk.
problems.root_cause: Separate tools for hiring, payroll and records.
problems.questions:
How many systems hold employee data?
How do you report headcount?
What takes the longest to find?

problems.problem: Senior hires are confidential, slow and costly when they go wrong.
problems.impact: Leadership gaps stall strategy and push work onto interim cover.
problems.root_cause: Reliance on personal networks and visible adverts that miss passive leaders, and a brief that is not yet clear.
problems.questions:
Which leadership seat is open or likely to open this year?
How confidential does the search need to be?
What would a wrong hire at this level cost you?

problems.problem: Succession planning for senior roles is thin.
problems.impact: A sudden departure leaves a gap with no ready successor.
problems.root_cause: Succession discussed informally and never reviewed.
problems.questions:
Who is the successor to each senior post?
When did you last review?
What would you do tomorrow if one of them left?

problems.problem: Boards struggle to attract non-executive and senior talent.
problems.impact: Missing skills at the top table.
problems.root_cause: Narrow networks and unclear role expectations.
problems.questions:
What skills is the board missing?
How do you currently find candidates?
What do you offer them?

problems.problem: Interim cover drags on and costs more.
problems.impact: High day rates and no long-term leadership.
problems.root_cause: Permanent search started late or lost momentum.
problems.questions:
How long has your interim been in place?
What is the permanent plan?
What does it cost per month?

problems.problem: Senior hires fail in the first year.
problems.impact: The cost of a wrong appointment and lost trust.
problems.root_cause: Poor fit assessment and no integration plan.
problems.questions:
Which senior hires in the last five years did not work out?
What was the cause?
How did you onboard them?

problems.problem: Confidential searches leak or stall.
problems.impact: Disruption and exposure.
problems.root_cause: Too many people involved and an unclear process.
problems.questions:
Who needs to know about the search?
How will you keep it private?
What is your timeline?

problems.problem: Drivers and warehouse staff are scarce, and licence, CPC and ADR requirements narrow the pool further.
problems.impact: Missed deliveries, expensive agency drivers and vehicles standing idle.
problems.root_cause: Licence and compliance checks late in the process, and pay or shift patterns that do not compete.
problems.questions:
How many vehicles are standing because there is no driver?
What do you pay for agency driver cover?
How long does it take to get a new driver compliant and on the road?

problems.problem: HGV driver shortages push wages and agency rates up.
problems.impact: Higher cost per mile and refused contracts.
problems.root_cause: Ageing drivers and few new entrants.
problems.questions:
How many drivers are you short?
What do you pay for agency cover?
How old is your driver base?

problems.problem: Warehouse staff turnover is high.
problems.impact: Training cost and picking errors.
problems.root_cause: Repetitive work, shifts and pay that lags the next warehouse.
problems.questions:
What is your warehouse turnover?
Where do leavers go?
What do you offer beyond pay?

problems.problem: Transport managers carry too much responsibility alone.
problems.impact: Compliance risk if the manager is away.
problems.root_cause: One person holds all the operator licence knowledge.
problems.questions:
Who covers your transport manager?
When was your last compliance review?
How is knowledge shared?

problems.problem: Seasonal peaks catch operations short.
problems.impact: Late deliveries and agency premiums.
problems.root_cause: Peak staffing planned too late.
problems.questions:
When does your peak start?
How early do you hire?
What did last peak cost?

problems.problem: Forklift and equipment operators with current tickets are hard to find.
problems.impact: Delays and extra training cost.
problems.root_cause: Training tickets not funded or tracked.
problems.questions:
How many operators hold valid tickets?
When do they expire?
Who pays for training?
